subject: Anthony Clark
title: Anthony Clark death: 'Yes, Dear' star and comedian dies at 62
answer: Anthony Clark, the stand-up comedian best known as Greg Warner on the CBS sitcom "Yes, Dear," died Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026, at 62. His former co-star Mike O'Malley announced the death, and his manager, Barry Katz, confirmed it. Deadline reported he died of complications from pneumonia.
in_the_news: News of his death spread Nov. 11–12 as O'Malley and fellow comedians posted tributes, sending fans back to "Yes, Dear" and his Boston comedy roots.
body:
Clark built his career in stand-up. A Virginia native and Emerson College graduate, he won a national college comedy award in 1986 and became a sellout draw in Boston's comedy clubs. That led to film roles in "Dogfight," "The Thing Called Love" and "The Rock," and to his own NBC sitcom, "Boston Common" (1996–1997), followed by "Soul Man" with Dan Aykroyd.

His biggest success was "Yes, Dear," which ran six seasons on CBS from 2000 to 2006 and 122 episodes. Clark played Greg, the uptight husband whose household is upended when his wife's sister moves in with her family, including O'Malley's character, Jimmy. In 2006 Clark also hosted the fourth season of NBC's "Last Comic Standing."

O'Malley called him a "hilarious guy" writing that he was a fan of Clark before they became friends, and added that the two had last spoken by phone about three weeks earlier. Comedian Nick Swardson called Clark one of his best friends, and Katz called him one of the funniest and most talented comedian-actors he had worked with.

faq.a: Deadline reported he died of complications from pneumonia. His manager did not give further details.

faq.q: Who did Anthony Clark play on 'Yes, Dear'?
faq.a: Greg Warner, the straitlaced husband, opposite Jean Louisa Kelly as his wife, Kim, and Mike O'Malley as his brother-in-law, Jimmy.

faq.q: What else was Anthony Clark in?
faq.a: His NBC sitcom "Boston Common," the films "The Rock" and "Dogfight," and "Last Comic Standing," which he hosted in 2006.
